_: A second repository, to test the portability claim rather than assert it.
This audits `samusmylove47-maker/eql-source` — a static-site generator in Python with no
shared code, no shared language and no shared test runner with the repository this config
lives in. It is kept here rather than there because findings go to that repository's session
through the Director, never into its tree by this one.
Point `root` at a clone:
git clone https://github.com/samusmylove47-maker/eql-source /somewhere
python3 tools/check-audit/audit.py tools/check-audit/checks.eql-source.json
Run against 2aeac48b. Every damage below is aimed at what a check says it guards, because
that repository is prose and data — generic operators reach almost none of it, which is the
portability boundary this file exists to document.

checks.name: check.py: a zone the dungeon index does not link

damages.label: drop every link to a zone
damages._: count=1 left `../dungeons/mistmoore.html` in place, so the zone was still linked and only the broken-link check fired. The attribution regex caught that as 'red, but not on this check', which is the tool working.

checks.name: check.py: the tier badge system in site.css

damages.label: site.css loses .t3 entirely
damages._: Replacing one occurrence with `.t3-renamed` left `.t3` present as a substring and produced a false DEAD against a live check. The check is `if cls not in css`, so the damage must remove every occurrence.

checks.name: check.py: a raid page loading a CDN script
checks.expect_failure: loads a script from a CDN

checks.name: check.py: a zone with an open gate that does not name it

damages.label: blank a verify_gate on a partial zone

checks.expect_failure: does not say which gate is open
_: NOT AUDITABLE FROM HERE, and this is a finding rather than a verdict.
check.py compares public/ against its sources and fails with `public/ is stale` the moment
any source file changes. Damaging assets/zones-index.json therefore trips staleness before
any assertion that reads the data, and masks every one of them. Auditing a data-driven check
in a repository with a build step needs the build re-run between damage and check — and
./build.sh needs Python 3.12, while this container has 3.11.15.
Left in deliberately so the audit reports it rather than quietly skipping it.

checks.name: check.py: the five source tiers on the home page  [KNOWN DEAD]
_: check.py:116 guards `index.html` at the repository ROOT. The site moved to public/ and
that path has not existed since. The whole block — the five-tier check at :124 and the
badge warning at :127 — has never run. The damage below removes a tier name from the
page a reader actually gets, which is exactly what the check says it prevents.

damages.label: remove a tier name from the home page
damages._: `Aggregator-removed` still CONTAINS `Aggregator`, and the check is `if t.lower() in h.lower()` — a substring test. The tool's superstring caution flagged it.

checks.expect_failure: names only \d+ of the 5 source tiers

checks.name: check.py: a published verified-count the data does not support  [KNOWN DEAD]
_: check.py:88 searches every home/index page for `(\d+) verified to the full three-gate
standard`. That phrase is on 0 of 723 pages, so `claim` is always None and the comparison
never runs. Unreached, not broken — and a green run cannot tell the two apart.
The first attempt at this reported ALIVE: changing a verify_level did make check.py go red,
but on a DIFFERENT assertion. `expect_failure` now requires the message this check owns.
